title: Du Moulin: the blessed know the Church is pressed, and so are concerned for it
source_text: XLVIII. Nec alia mens est Petri Molinaei. Beati spiritus, inquit, etsi non videant quae hic fiunt, nec norint singulos, sciunt tamen Ecclesiam premi ab adversariis, & ei proposita esse perpetua certamina. Cumque ex glorificatione aucta potius sit quam imminuta eorum charitas, consentaneum est eos de Ecclesia militante esse sollicitos. In Thesauro Thesium Sedanensium Tom. 1. Thesibus de Sanctis part. 3. th. 3.
pass_a_gloss: Nor is the mind of Peter du Moulin otherwise. The blessed spirits, he says, although they do not see the things that happen here, nor know individuals, nevertheless know that the Church is pressed by adversaries, and that perpetual contests are set before it. And since from glorification their charity has been increased rather than diminished, it is consonant that they are anxious about the militant Church. In the Treasury of Sedan Theses, volume 1, in the Theses on the Saints, part 3, thesis 3.
pass_b_english: Peter du Moulin is of the same mind. "The blessed spirits," he says, "do not see what happens here and do not know individuals, yet they know that the Church is hard pressed by its enemies and faces endless struggles. Since glorification has increased their love rather than lessened it, it is fitting that they should be concerned for the Church Militant." (Treasury of Sedan Theses, volume 1, Theses on the Saints, part 3, thesis 3.)

lemmas.latin: ex glorificatione aucta potius quam imminuta
lemmas.gloss: increased rather than diminished by glorification

choices.why: Du Moulin claims general solicitude, not active intercession for individuals; 'concerned' keeps that limit.
